explanation: Count each age and assign a disjoint destination segment of that length. Track the next unfilled slot for each age. Repeatedly swap a person into the next free slot of their own segment and advance or remove that age’s offset.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time using hashing. Counting/bucketing scans n records; each write or slot-filling swap permanently places one record. Hash operations are expected constant time.
spaceComplexity: O(u) auxiliary hash entries for u distinct ages; the original people array supplies all storage for records. Bucket variants retain n records; offset/count variants retain one map entry per distinct age.

correctness: Each age’s unfilled segment has exactly as many slots as remaining people of that age. A swap puts one person in a valid final slot, reduces that count by one and preserves every record. Each iteration permanently fills one slot, so termination yields contiguous age groups without losing or duplicating anyone.
walkthrough: For [(6,Nyx),(2,Bo),(6,Ana)], suppose age 6 gets slots 0..1 and age 2 gets slot 2. Fill slot 0 with Nyx. The person Bo at slot 1 belongs in slot 2, so swap Bo and Ana and finish age 2. Ana now fills slot 1. The wrapper accepts [(6,Nyx),(6,Ana),(2,Bo)]; hash iteration may choose another valid group order.
edgeCases: Repeated names still represent separate people and must be preserved.
A single age already forms a valid group.
Group order is unrestricted, so compare structure and membership rather than one fixed sorted order.
